name: Joel

overview.author: Joel son of Pethuel (1:1). Nothing else is known about him.
overview.date: Uncertain. Proposals range from the 9th century BC to after the exile (about 400 BC); the book’s message does not depend on a precise date.
overview.audience: The people of Judah and Jerusalem, including priests and elders.
overview.setting: A devastating locust plague and drought have ruined the land, and Joel sees in it a warning of the coming day of the LORD.
overview.purpose: To call God’s people to wholehearted repentance in light of the day of the LORD, and to promise restoration, the outpouring of the Spirit, and final judgment on the nations.
overview.structure: The locust plague and call to lament (1), the coming day of the LORD and the call to return (2:1–17), and God’s response: restoration, the Spirit, and judgment of the nations (2:18–3:21).

themes.title: The Day of the LORD
themes.text: A day of judgment and salvation, darkness for the unrepentant but refuge for God’s people.

themes.title: Repentance
themes.text: “Rend your hearts and not your garments” (2:13). God wants inward, not merely outward, sorrow.

themes.title: God’s Character
themes.text: “Gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love” (2:13).

themes.title: Restoration
themes.text: “I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten” (2:25).

themes.title: The Spirit Poured Out
themes.text: God will pour out His Spirit on all flesh, regardless of age, gender, or status.

themes.title: Salvation by Calling on the LORD
themes.text: “Everyone who calls on the name of the LORD shall be saved” (2:32).

keyVerses.quote: Return to me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping, and with mourning.
Rend your hearts and not your garments.
I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten.
I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh.
Everyone who calls on the name of the LORD shall be saved.

christInBook.text: Peter declares that Pentecost fulfills Joel’s prophecy of the Spirit poured out through the risen Christ (Acts 2:16–21, 33).
Paul applies “everyone who calls on the name of the Lord” to faith in Jesus (Romans 10:13).
The LORD roaring from Zion as refuge anticipates Christ as both judge and shelter.

crossReferences.note: Calling on the Lord for salvation.
The great day of the LORD.

reflection: What would it look like for you to “rend your heart and not your garments” (2:13)?
What “years the locust has eaten” do you need to trust God to redeem (2:25)?
How does the gift of the Spirit to “all flesh” encourage you in serving God?
How should the coming day of the Lord shape the way you live now?
Who in your life needs to hear that everyone who calls on the Lord will be saved?

chapterList.title: The Locust Plague
chapterList.summary: Joel describes an unprecedented locust invasion that has stripped vines, fig trees, and fields. Drunkards, priests, and farmers all mourn. Joel calls a fast and a solemn assembly: “Alas for the day! For the day of the LORD is near.”
questions: Why does Joel say to tell this to future generations (1:3)?
What does the plague do to worship (1:9, 13)?
How can natural disasters call us to seek God?

chapterList.title: Return to Me with All Your Heart
chapterList.summary: An army like locusts advances; the day of the LORD is great and very awesome. “Yet even now... return to me with all your heart... Rend your hearts and not your garments.” God responds with pity, restores what the locusts ate, and promises to pour out His Spirit on all flesh. Everyone who calls on His name will be saved.
questions: What does “even now” (2:12) say about God’s patience?
What does God promise to restore (2:25–27)?
What does it mean to call on the name of the Lord?

chapterList.title: The Valley of Decision
chapterList.summary: God gathers the nations to the Valley of Jehoshaphat for judgment because they scattered His people. “Beat your plowshares into swords.” Multitudes gather in the valley of decision. The LORD roars from Zion, but He is a refuge to His people. The mountains will drip sweet wine, and the LORD dwells in Zion.
questions: What comfort does 3:16–18 give God’s people?

tagline: The day of the LORD and the outpouring of the Spirit
readingPlan: 3 chapters: one chapter a day takes 3 days; two a day takes about 2 days. For each chapter, read it on ESV.org, then come back here for the summary, questions, and your notes.
